_comment: Authored summary targets — plan.md §9. Keyed by dataset record id. Kept separate from dataset.jsonl so regenerating the dataset never destroys authoring. Merge with: npm --prefix api run merge:dataset
_batch: 001 — first pass across all four bands, both free-text scripts, and both contradiction cases. For voice review before the full set.
red_cauda_equina-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain with leg pain and numbness for 6 weeks to 3 months, gradual onset.

**Key findings**
- Saddle numbness reported — inner thighs and the area he sits on
- Pain radiates below the knee; 5/10, relieved by lying down
- Bladder and bowel control both reported intact
- No leg weakness, no foot drag, walking unrestricted
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Saddle sensory change alone triggers the cauda equina screen. The reassuring bladder, bowel and power answers do not override it.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- When the saddle numbness began, and whether it is spreading
- Urinary hesitancy, poor stream, or loss of the sensation of bladder filling — the yes/no question misses early change
- Whether the numbness crosses the midline
- Perianal sensation and anal tone on examination
red_myelopathy-000:
**Snapshot** — 46y woman, teacher. Neck pain with arm pain and numbness for 3 to 12 months, getting worse.

**Key findings**
- Fine-motor loss — buttoning, picking up a coin and writing all harder
- Both hands affected; objects slip from the grip
- Pain and numbness below the elbow into the hand
- Now needs some help with dressing and bathing
- Gait reported steady; no urinary urgency

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Loss of hand dexterity with bilateral involvement suggests a pattern consistent with cord compression rather than a single nerve root. The root-level features are present too, but the bilateral hand signs are what raise the urgency.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Hoffmann's, inverted supinator, and lower-limb reflexes
- Whether anyone else noticed the handwriting change first
- Any band-like tightness around the trunk
- How quickly function has declined over the last month
red_fragility_fracture-000:
**Snapshot** — 74y woman, homemaker. Lower back pain for 2 to 6 weeks with no clear cause, 8/10.

**Key findings**
- Severe pain of recent onset with no injury reported
- Known brittle bones
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Relieved by lying down; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Sudden severe pain without trauma, at 74 with osteoporosis, raises a query of vertebral fragility fracture. An acute mechanical pattern also matched; the fracture query outranks it.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Whether the pain began during an ordinary movement — bending, coughing, standing from a chair
- Any height loss or new stoop noticed by family
- Point tenderness over a spinous process
- Steroid use and any previous fragility fracture
amber_lumbar_radiculopathy-001:
**Snapshot** — 58y man, Nashik. Lower back and leg pain with numbness for 3 to 12 months, 7/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain radiates below the knee on the right
- Numbness and tingling in the leg; worse on coughing and straining
- Worse sitting, relieved lying down; walking unrestricted
- No weakness and no red flags
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Below-knee radiation with numbness and a positive cough response, present well beyond six weeks, fits a lumbar nerve-root pattern.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- He wrote *(translated)*: "I have been suffering for a long time. I have to work and I cannot bear the pain either." Ability to keep working may matter more to him than the diagnosis.
- Straight-leg raise and dermatomal mapping
- What his work involves, and which movements provoke the leg pain
- Whether structured physiotherapy has ever been offered
amber_stenosis-000:
**Snapshot** — 62y man, retired. Lower back and bilateral leg pain with difficulty walking, more than a year.

**Key findings**
- Walking limited to 100–500 metres
- Relief on sitting or bending forward, not on standing still
- Pain to the buttocks on both sides; nothing below the knee
- No numbness, weakness or red flags
- Painkillers only; no physiotherapy yet

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Walking-limited pain relieved by flexion, at 62, fits a neurogenic claudication pattern. Conservative care has not been attempted.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Walking distance on the flat versus uphill, and whether cycling is easier
- Peripheral pulses and ankle-brachial index, to exclude a vascular cause
- Whether standing still alone ever settles it
- Any night cramps or rest pain in the feet
amber_post_surgical-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for more than a year, 5/10, no radiation.

**Key findings**
- Previous L4–L5 discectomy in 2019 in Mumbai, per his own note
- Pain stays in the back — no leg symptoms, numbness or weakness
- Physiotherapy for 2 to 6 weeks, partial benefit
- Worse on prolonged sitting, relieved lying down
- No red flags; no imaging since the surgery

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Previous spine surgery makes this a revision assessment rather than a first presentation, whatever the current symptom severity.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Whether this pain resembles the pre-operative pain or is different in character
- How long he was pain-free after surgery before symptoms returned
- Operative notes and any post-operative imaging
- Whether the physiotherapy was supervised and completed
grey_hip-000:
**Snapshot** — 66y woman, homemaker. Lower back pain for more than a year, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain is groin-dominant rather than back-dominant
- Hip stiffness putting on socks and getting out of a car
- Radiation stops at the buttock; nothing below the knee
- No numbness, weakness or red flags
- Painkillers only; no physiotherapy

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Groin-dominant pain with hip stiffness on dressing, and no radiation past the buttock, points away from the spine and towards the hip joint.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Internal rotation range, and whether it reproduces the groin pain
- Whether pain is worst on weight-bearing or on the first steps after rest
- Any hip X-ray already taken elsewhere
- Whether the back pain and the groin pain began together or separately
grey_vascular-000:
**Snapshot** — 64y man, shop or business. Leg pain and difficulty walking for 3 to 12 months.

**Key findings**
- Walking limited to 100–500 metres, both legs
- Pain settles on standing still alone — no need to sit or bend forward
- Diabetes and tobacco use
- Radiation stops at the buttock; no numbness or weakness
- No red flags

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Relief on standing still, without needing to flex, is the discriminator separating this from spinal claudication. With diabetes and smoking alongside it, a vascular cause is the stronger query.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Peripheral pulses and ankle-brachial index
- Whether the claudication distance is consistent day to day
- Any rest pain, night pain in the foot, or slow-healing ulcers
- Smoking history in pack-years
grey_unclear-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Selected "none of these" as the main complaint, so the questionnaire never showed the spine branches.

**Key findings**
- No spinal complaint selected
- All ten red-flag questions answered no
- No other medical conditions reported
- The back, neck, function and treatment sections were never reached, so there is no symptom detail to review

**Supporting the triage verdict** — The complaint does not match any spine pattern the questionnaire can route on. This is a gap in the intake rather than a clinical finding.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What the problem actually is, in the patient's own words
- Whether "none of these" was genuine, or the option list did not fit
- Whether the referral was for something the form does not cover
- Whether it is worth re-taking the form once the complaint is clear
green_untreated_chronic-012:
**Snapshot** — 55y woman, Pune. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Worse on prolonged sitting, relieved lying down
- Painkillers only — no physiotherapy, injections or surgery
- No red flags

**Supporting the triage verdict** — More than six weeks of pain with no neurological findings, and structured conservative care not yet attempted.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- She wrote *(translated)*: "I don't understand what I should do. I will do whatever you tell me." She is likely to accept a physiotherapy plan if it is explained clearly.
- What she believes is causing the pain
- Daily activities and lifting demands at home
- Whether supervised physiotherapy is accessible to her locally
contra_multiselect-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10, no radiation.

**Key findings**
- Pain stays in the back; no numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted, sleep undisturbed
- Three multi-select answers contradict themselves
- Treatment, imaging and comorbidity history are all unreliable as recorded

**Supporting the triage verdict** — On the answers that are internally consistent, this is six weeks or more of uncomplicated back pain with no neurological findings. Note the verdict assumes conservative care has not been tried, and that is one of the contradicted fields.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What has actually been tried — "nothing yet" was ticked alongside painkillers and rest
- Whether an X-ray exists — "no scans done" was ticked alongside X-ray
- Whether he has diabetes — "none of these" was ticked alongside diabetes
- Whether someone helped him complete the form
contra_all_red_flags-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 9/10, has stopped working.

**Key findings**
- Yes to nine of ten red flags, including bladder, bowel and saddle symptoms
- Also progressive weakness, fever, cancer history and weight loss
- Yet non-radiating pain, no leg numbness or weakness, unrestricted walking
- Night pain waking him, yet sleep reported never disturbed
- A recent fall, yet onset described as gradual

**Supporting the triage verdict** — The bladder, bowel and saddle answers route this to emergency regardless of the rest. The answer set is not internally coherent.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Verify the bladder, bowel and saddle answers directly before acting
- Reconcile night pain against undisturbed sleep, and the fall against gradual onset
- Whether the questions were understood as asked
- Do not stand down the emergency pathway on suspicion of over-reporting alone
